title: Habitability, population capacity and growth

provenance.location: TOPICPOS 1837221 (0x001c08a5), HLP file offset 464538 (0x0007169a), topic 284 'Growth Conditions'
TOPICPOS 1853471 (0x001c481f), HLP file offset 468500 (0x00072614), topic 285 'Maximum Population Growth'

provenance.note: Maximum population from habitability; 100% supports 1,000,000; plateau after 25% capacity.

provenance.location: TOPICPOS 2326597 (0x00238045), HLP file offset 585274 (0x0008ee3a), topic 349 'Annual Growth Rate'
provenance.note: Annual growth = habitability value x maximum growth rate.

setup.baseline: A planet with known gravity, temperature and radiation inside the race range.
setup.variable: Habitability value, population and growth rate.

procedure: Record the home world environment, habitability value, population and growth rate.
Colonize a controlled planet and record population each year until the cap.
Repeat with races at minimum, middle and maximum growth rates.
Test negative habitability, immunity to one factor, and Hyper-Expansion.
Record deaths and growth separately from terraforming changes.

documented: Maximum population is proportional to habitability value; 100% supports 1,000,000 (documented-only).
Annual growth is the habitability value times the maximum growth rate, and plateaus after 25% capacity (documented-only).
Planets with negative habitability kill colonists at habitability/10 percent per year (documented-only).

unresolved: Exact growth-curve shape after the 25% plateau is not stated.
Rounding and cap application with Hyper-Expansion are unknown.
The help does not establish whether immunity makes the factor exactly 100% for all calculations.
